**Step 1 — Scene:** A plate of stir-fried noodles with beef and mixed vegetables. I’m estimating the main noodle plate only, excluding the separate side plates and drinks.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A shallow disposable plate, approximately **23 cm** in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 11.5² ≈ **415 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Yellow noodles, beef strips, mixed vegetables (mainly cabbage, with carrot and green vegetables), and a glossy sauce/oil coating.

**Steps 4–6 — Area, volume, and weight:** The food covers approximately **71%** of the plate. Component areas partition the mixed pile; the coating occupies no additional footprint.

| Item | Plate area covered | Area | Typical height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked noodles | 43% | 178 cm² | 1.9 cm | 338 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 270 g |
| Mixed vegetables | 18% | 75 cm² | 1.9 cm | 143 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 86 g |
| Beef strips | 10% | 42 cm² | 1.5 cm | 63 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 60 g |

The visible coating is harder to measure: approximately **15 ml of sauce → 15 g**, plus **6 ml of oil → 5 g**. These are estimated separately rather than adding another layer of plate coverage.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Using cooked-weight values: noodles 150 kcal/100 g, vegetables 35, beef 230, sauce 60, and oil 880. This gives approximately **626 kcal**.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **436 g and 626 kcal** is plausible for this substantial but not overflowing noodle plate. The largest uncertainty is the amount of oil in the stir-fry.
